structured_output.title: Results screen (S5)
structured_output.summary: Add `src/ui/results-screen.ts` (+ CSS) and have `createRaceUi` show it instead of the Phase 0 finish panel when the player finishes. It has a solid navy ground, the triple stripe, a "RACE COMPLETE · N LAPS" label, the track name, a rally-red placing roundel, a mustard best-lap chip, a POS/DRIVER/TIME/GAP table with rows dealt 40 ms apart and the player's row in rally-red, plus RETRY and NEXT RACE. `game.ts` wires NEXT RACE to a new `nextTrackId` in `src/content/tracks.ts`, which wraps. Existing tests can't be edited, so: leave `finish-panel.ts` in place, keep `createRaceUi(root, { onRaceAgain })` and the 3-arg `reset(laps, outline, colours)` valid (new inputs like `onNextRace`, track name and car numbers are optional), and give the results root the `ui-finish` class too.

acceptanceCriteria.text: After `reset(3, outline, ['rally-red','mustard'], …)` with track name 'Dust Bowl', a `phase: 'finished'` sync shows a visible `.ui-results` screen containing a triple stripe of exactly 3 stripe elements, the label "Race complete · 3 laps" (case-insensitive), the text 'Dust Bowl' and a mustard best-lap chip with the player's best lap (lapTicks [2500,2400,2300] → '0:38.33').

The results table has the header cells POS, DRIVER, TIME and GAP and one row per car, in finishing order. Each row shows its position, a driver label ('YOU · #1' for car 0, 'CPU · #n' for a bot, where n is that car's livery number, e.g. 'CPU · #7') and the time `formatTime` gives for its finishTick (7200 ticks → '2:00.00').

GAP reads '–' (en dash) for the leader. Every other finished car shows its time minus the leader's as '+s.cc', or '+m:ss.cc' at 60 s or more. Example: leader finishTick 7200 and the next car 7237 gives '+0.62'; a car 4200 ticks behind gives '+1:10.00'.

A car that hasn't finished when the screen opens is listed after the finished cars, with TIME and GAP both '–:––.––'. A later sync where it has finished fills in its time and gap. Syncs where nothing changed make no DOM mutations under the results screen.

Exactly one row (the player's) has the modifier class `ui-results__row--player`. Row i (0-based, in table order) has the inline custom property `--ui-deal-index: i`, which the CSS multiplies by the 40 ms stagger token.

The placing roundel shows the player's position as an ordinal: '1ST' when the player wins, '2ND' when the player finishes behind the bot. A new exported `ordinal(n)` in `src/ui/format.ts` returns 1→'1ST', 2→'2ND', 3→'3RD', 4→'4TH', 11→'11TH', 12→'12TH', 13→'13TH', 21→'21ST', 22→'22ND'.

The results screen has a RETRY button that calls `onRaceAgain` and a NEXT RACE button that calls a new `onNextRace` option, each exactly once per click. NEXT RACE has focus when the screen opens. After reset() and a second finish, the table holds only the new race's rows (one per car). No inline style or SVG paint attribute sets a colour.

`nextTrackId(currentId, ids?)` exported from `src/content/tracks.ts` returns the id after `currentId` in `ids` (default: registered TRACKS order) and wraps from the last back to the first. ['a','b','c']: 'a'→'b', 'c'→'a'. With the real registry, 'dust-bowl'→'dust-bowl'. An unknown id throws.
